title: Classiq Launches Fault Tolerance Engine for Hardware-Aware Quantum Application Synthesis - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Classiq added a Fault Tolerance Engine to its SDK that compiles logical circuits (Qmod or Clifford+T QASM) into 3D surface-code lattice-surgery execution plans with physical qubit and error estimates, replacing static resource formulas. It routed a 219-logical-qubit, ~2.5M-gate chemistry workload in about an hour; QLDPC and color code support is in development.

insights.claim: Classiq's Fault Tolerance Engine maps high-level logical quantum circuits into concrete 3D spatial-temporal execution plans on fault-tolerant QPUs, producing hardware-aware routing schedules, magic-state cultivation plans and empirical physical qubit and error-rate estimates instead of static algorithmic resource formulas.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Software that sizes real FTQC hardware requirements positions Classiq as a design tool for hardware makers, not just app developers.
insights.quote: By moving beyond static algorithmic resource formulas, the engine generates hardware-aware routing schedules, magic-state cultivation plans, and empirical physical qubit and error-rate estimates.

insights.claim: The engine routed a tensor hypercontraction chemistry workload of 219 logical qubits and roughly 2.5-2.6 million logical gates (~1.3M CX gates) in about one hour.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Demonstrates compilation tooling can already handle utility-scale chemistry circuits ahead of hardware availability.
insights.locator: Classiq Fault Tolerance Engine Technical Specifications

insights.claim: By producing complete execution plans before fault-tolerant QPUs exist, the engine lets developers and hardware teams identify physical resource bottlenecks such as magic state factories, optimize code distance and determine real hardware requirements.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: More realistic resource estimates could reset market expectations for when quantum advantage in chemistry is reachable.

insights.claim: The engine currently supports only 3D surface codes but is modality-agnostic across hardware supporting surface-code QEC, including superconducting, neutral atom, trapped ion and silicon spin qubits, with customizable noise models.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A hardware-neutral software layer hedges the modality race, letting Classiq benefit regardless of which qubit technology wins.

insights.claim: Classiq is developing support for QLDPC and color codes, signaling that error-correction schemes beyond the surface code are becoming commercially relevant.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QLDPC adoption could sharply cut physical qubit overhead, changing which hardware roadmaps look competitive.
insights.quote: Development is underway to extend support to Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) and color codes.
